params.c: The credential: a wallet or a passkey (see `Credential`).
params.owners: The first owner set, in order: exactly one credential for an account to be created with it; `saltOf` and `addressOf` compute any set's.
params.nonce: The signing credential's next record-change nonce (`recordNonceOf`): each signature is accepted once.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds: the call reverts after it.
params.due: When the pending change being cancelled takes effect, as the contract recorded it: it names that change, so a cancellation needs no nonce.
params.signature: A credential's signature over the EIP-712 message: `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.
params.configHash: The hash of the strategy contract's configuration, as the owner signed it.
params.domain: A chain, by Circle's CCTP domain number (Ethereum 0, Avalanche 1, OP Mainnet 2, Arbitrum 3, Base 6, Polygon 7, HyperEVM 19).
params.id: An authorisation's id: a counter per account, given by `authoriseStrategy` at the home and the same on every chain.
params.vaultKey: The key of an allowance, as `vaultKey` computes it from the factory, the strategy id and the configuration hash.
params.digest: The EIP-712 digest that was signed (see `hashTypedData`).
params.structHash: The EIP-712 hash of the signed struct.
params.user: The user's id: a UUID, left-padded to 32 bytes.

types.Credential: One owner credential. A wallet: `kind` 1, `x` its address left-padded, `y` zero. A passkey: `kind` 2, `x` and `y` the coordinates of its P-256 public key.
types.StrategyGrant: The owner's authorisation to fund one strategy contract: `allowance` of USDC on the chain of `domain`, for the contract of `vaultFactory` with `strategyId` and `configHash`. Every field is signed; `nonce` is the signing credential's record-change nonce and `deadline` the signature's expiry.
types.Withdrawal: A withdrawal the owner signs, every field included: `amount` of `token` (zero: the native coin) to `to`, with at most `maxFee` of it to `feeRecipient`. `to` and `feeRecipient` must still be the withdrawal address and the factory's fee recipient in effect when it executes. `nonce` is the signing credential's nonce on this chain and `deadline` the signature's expiry.
types.Grant: An authorisation the home accepted, as `grant` returns it: the factory, the chain, whether its allowance was applied, the strategy id, the configuration hash, the allowance, and the trust epoch it was granted under (a cancelled trust voids it).
types.Proposal: A version the recovery key proposed: `due`, when it may be accepted (zero: none pending), and `codeHash`, the implementation's code hash at the proposal, which acceptance checks again.

contracts.name: DepositAccount
contracts.title: The deposit contract
contracts.brief: Each user's own contract: their balance and their owner record, at the same address on every supported chain.
contracts.summary: Each user's own contract, at the same address on every supported chain. It holds the user's balance and the owner record: one to four credentials (passkeys or wallets) and the withdrawal address. The copy on Arbitrum is the **home**: every change to the record is signed and accepted there, waits 24 hours, and reaches the other chains' copies by a Circle message the home sends; a copy trusts the record it holds for 30 days after the home sent it, and the same record sent again renews it. Money leaves only to the withdrawal address, to a strategy contract the owner authorised (within the amount signed for), as a fee the owner signed, into the pinned USDT to USDC pool, or by Circle's bridge to this same address on another supported chain. There is no other call: no arbitrary call, no upgrade, no admin.

DELAY.does: How long an addition, a removal, a later withdrawal-address change and a new factory trust wait before they take effect. The first withdrawal address does not wait, nor DLTX's pinned vault factory's first trust on Arbitrum or HyperEVM.

RECORD_TTL.does: How long a copy trusts the owner record it holds after the home sent it: 30 days. Past it the copy reads as unsynced (no owner signature, no local action, no withdrawal, no withdrawal address) until the home's record arrives again, even unchanged. It bounds how long a credential removed or an address replaced at the home stays usable on a chain the change has not reached.

ADD_CREDENTIAL_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to add a credential.

REMOVE_CREDENTIAL_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to remove a credential.

SET_WITHDRAWAL_ADDRESS_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to set the withdrawal address.

CANCEL_REMOVAL_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to cancel a pending removal.

CANCEL_ADDITION_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to cancel a pending addition.

CANCEL_WITHDRAWAL_ADDRESS_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to cancel a pending withdrawal-address change.

WITHDRAW_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs for a signed withdrawal.

REVOKE_TRANSFER_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to revoke the transfer key on one chain.

ALLOW_TRANSFER_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to allow the transfer key again on one chain.

AUTHORISE_STRATEGY_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to authorise funding a strategy contract.

CANCEL_TRUST_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type the owner signs to cancel a factory's pending trust.

MAX_GRANT.does: The most one authorisation may grant (2^128 − 1), so no sum of them can overflow.

RECORD_TAG.does: Tags a message carrying the owner record, so no other message can be read as one.

AUTH_TAG.does: Tags a message carrying an authorisation from the home.

factory.does: The deposit factory that created this account; the account reads the transfer key, the fee recipient and the escape hatch's state from it.

transferRevoked.does: Whether the owner has revoked the transfer key on this chain.

recordPublishedAt.does: When the home sent the owner record this copy holds, as a Unix time in seconds; zero at the home and on a copy that has never received one. The copy is synced until this time plus `RECORD_TTL` (30 days).

allowance.does: What the transfer key may still pay one strategy contract in this chain's USDC, by the key `vaultKey` computes.

authorisationCount.does: How many authorisations the home has accepted; the last one's id.

authorisationApplied.does: On a copy: whether the authorisation with this id has been applied (each id applies once).

initialize.does: Sets the account's first owner set: one credential. Any further credential is an addition, which waits 24 hours.
initialize.who: The deposit factory only, in the transaction that creates the account.
checks: Exactly one credential, well-shaped: a non-zero address with `y` zero, or a point on P-256. So a second owner can never be hidden in the account's address.
No code is checked at a wallet's address here, so an account can always be created where money already waits; a wallet that is a contract could never sign anyway (ECDSA only).

isHome.does: Whether this copy is the home (this chain is Arbitrum).

synced.does: Whether this copy trusts its credentials: always at the home; on another chain while the home's record it last received was sent within the last 30 days (`RECORD_TTL`). A copy that has never received one, or whose record is older, accepts no owner signature, no local action and no withdrawal, and names no withdrawal address.

recordNonceOf.does: A credential's next record-change nonce (used at the home).

localNonceOf.does: A credential's next local-action nonce on this chain.

allowanceOf.does: What the transfer key may still pay the strategy contract of this factory, strategy and configuration, in this chain's USDC.

vaultKey.does: The key of an allowance: the hash of the factory, the strategy id and the configuration hash.

trustKey.does: The key of a factory's trust for one chain: the hash of the factory and the domain.

isTrusted.does: Whether this account trusts a strategy contract factory for a chain now (on a copy, for its own chain).

trustOf.does: When a factory's trust for a chain took or takes effect (zero: none, or cancelled) and how many times it was proposed.

returns.due: When the trust took or takes effect (0: untrusted, or cancelled).
returns.epoch: How many times this factory's trust for this chain was proposed.

grant.does: The home's authorisation with this id (zeros if none).

credentialId.does: A credential's id: the hash of its kind, `x` and `y`.

credentials.does: The credentials in effect now: an addition past its 24 hours counts, a removal past its 24 hours does not, settled in storage or not. On a copy not yet synced, the first owner set, which it does not trust.

withdrawalAddress.does: The withdrawal address in effect now: zero until the first one is set (it takes effect at once), the pending one once its 24 hours have passed, and zero on an unsynced copy (never reached, or its record older than 30 days).

pendingWithdrawalAddress.does: A withdrawal-address change still waiting for its 24 hours, and when it takes effect (zeros if none).

returns.next: The address that will become the withdrawal address (zero: no change pending).
returns.due: When it takes effect (0: none pending).

removalDue.does: When a credential's pending removal takes effect (zero: none, or already in effect).

additionDue.does: When a credential's pending addition takes effect (zero: none, or already in effect).

version.does: The owner record's version in effect now, counting changes past their 24 hours; a copy is up to date when its version equals the home's.

isCredential.does: Whether this credential is one in effect that this copy trusts: false on an unsynced copy, an expired one included.

isCredentialId.does: `isCredential` by the credential's id (`credentialId`): what a strategy contract keeps of the credential that signed an action it applies later, such as the Hyperliquid leg's agent choice. False on an unsynced copy.

params.id: The credential's id, the hash of its kind, `x` and `y` (`credentialId`).

domainSeparator.does: The EIP-712 domain of the owner's messages: name "DLTX Owner", version "1", this contract's address, and no chain id.

hashTypedData.does: The EIP-712 digest a credential signs, for a given struct hash, in this account's domain.

checkOwnerSignature.does: Whether a credential in effect, and trusted on this chain, signed this digest: false on an unsynced copy, an expired one included. Never reverts on a malformed signature. The strategy contracts and their factory check the owner's other messages through it.

addCredential.does: Proposes a new credential. It takes effect 24 hours later unless cancelled.
addCredential.who: The owner: a record change signed by a credential in effect, with that credential's own record nonce.
addCredential.when: At the home (Arbitrum) only, before the signature's deadline.
checks: A well-shaped credential not already in the set (a pending addition counts), and fewer than four counting pending additions.
A wallet must be a plain address: no contract code, except an EIP-7702 delegation, which still signs with its key.
Until it takes effect the new credential cannot sign, and any credential in effect may cancel it.

cancelAddition.who: The owner: signed by any credential in effect. No nonce: the message names the addition and its due time, so a replay can only cancel again.
cancelAddition.when: At the home only, before the addition takes effect and before the signature's deadline.

proposeRemoval.does: Proposes removing a credential. It takes effect 24 hours later unless cancelled.
proposeRemoval.who: The owner: a record change signed by ANOTHER credential in effect, with that credential's own record nonce.
proposeRemoval.when: At the home only, before the signature's deadline.
checks: The credential is in effect (a pending addition is cancelled, not removed), and no removal of it is already pending.
At least one credential always remains: removals already pending are counted.
A credential whose removal is pending still signs until it takes effect.

cancelRemoval.who: The owner: signed by any credential in effect except the one being removed. No nonce: the message names the removal and its due time.
cancelRemoval.when: At the home only, before the removal takes effect and before the signature's deadline.
checks: The one exception: the credential being removed may cancel its own removal when that removal would leave a single other credential standing (pending removals counted, except those it proposed itself). So a thief holding one of two credentials cannot win the account by proposing first.

The other side of that rule: with two credentials in all, neither can remove the other (a standoff). The way out is to withdraw everything to the withdrawal address in effect, exit every strategy, and open a new account; with at least two other credentials standing, a stolen one can be removed.

setWithdrawalAddress.does: Sets the withdrawal address. The first one, while none has ever been in effect, takes effect at once. A later one is proposed and takes effect 24 hours later unless cancelled; a new proposal replaces a pending one and restarts its 24 hours.
setWithdrawalAddress.who: The owner: a record change signed by a credential in effect, with that credential's own record nonce.
setWithdrawalAddress.when: At the home only, before the signature's deadline.
checks: A non-zero address.

cancelWithdrawalAddress.does: Cancels a pending withdrawal-address change. The first address is never pending, so it cannot be cancelled.
cancelWithdrawalAddress.who: The owner: signed by any credential in effect. No nonce: the message names the address and its due time.
cancelWithdrawalAddress.when: At the home only, strictly before the change takes effect, and before the signature's deadline.

params.next: The pending withdrawal address being cancelled.

publish.does: Sends the owner record in effect (credentials, withdrawal address, version, and the time it was sent) to this same address on another chain, by a Circle message: no burn, no fee, finalized. Sending an unchanged record renews that copy for another 30 days (`RECORD_TTL`).
publish.who: Anyone: the owner can keep a copy current, or renew it, without DLTX.
publish.when: At the home only, to any domain but Arbitrum's own. Changes past their 24 hours are settled first, and a pending addition is never sent.

handleReceiveFinalizedMessage.does: Receives the home's message at a copy: either the owner record, which replaces the copy's credentials, withdrawal address and version and renews the copy for 30 days from the time the home sent it, or an authorisation, which adds its allowance and trusts its factory on this chain. A message it does not take is ignored without reverting, so it cannot block the next one.
handleReceiveFinalizedMessage.who: Circle's message transmitter, delivering a message that this same address sent from Arbitrum. Anyone may relay Circle's attested message to the transmitter.
handleReceiveFinalizedMessage.when: On a copy only (never at the home), at the finalized threshold.
checks: Sent from domain 3 (Arbitrum) by this same address.

A record: its first is taken at any version if the home sent it at or after this copy's deployment; after that, a strictly higher version, or the same version sent later than the one held, which renews the copy (`RECORD_TTL`). An older version, or one sent no later than the record held, is ignored. One to four well-shaped credentials.

An authorisation: only once the copy holds a record (otherwise it reverts, so the message can be relayed again later), and each id once. A non-zero factory and configuration, on a chain with Circle USDC. The allowance adds up, saturating rather than overflowing.

params.sourceDomain: The CCTP domain the message comes from: only the home's, Arbitrum (3), is accepted.
params.sender: The address that sent the message, as 32 bytes: only this same account at the home is accepted.
params.finalityThresholdExecuted: The finality the message was attested at: only a finalized message is taken.
params.messageBody: The home's message: its owner record and version, or an authorisation.

handleReceiveUnfinalizedMessage.does: Circle's handler for an unfinalized message: always refuses, since this contract accepts finalized messages only.

revokeTransfer.does: Revokes the transfer key on this chain: it can no longer withdraw, fund, convert or bridge from this account here. Signed withdrawals and the escape hatch still work.
revokeTransfer.who: The owner: a local action signed by a credential in effect, naming this chain, with that credential's own local nonce here.
revokeTransfer.when: On any chain whose copy is synced, before the signature's deadline. Takes effect at once.

params.nonce: The signing credential's next nonce on this chain (`localNonceOf`): each signature is accepted once.

allowTransfer.does: Allows the transfer key again on this chain.
allowTransfer.who: The owner: a local action, as `revokeTransfer`.
allowTransfer.when: On any chain whose copy is synced, before the signature's deadline. Takes effect at once.

params.nonce: The signing credential's next nonce on this chain (`localNonceOf`): each signature is accepted once.

authoriseStrategy.does: Authorises funding one strategy contract: an amount of USDC on one supported chain, for the contract of one factory, strategy id and configuration hash. It gets an id. A factory not yet trusted for that chain becomes trusted 24 hours after the first authorisation naming it, cancellable until then, except DLTX's pinned vault factory on Arbitrum or HyperEVM, trusted at once (for Arbitrum, the amount is then added in the same call).
authoriseStrategy.who: The owner: a local action signed by a credential in effect, with that credential's own local nonce.
authoriseStrategy.when: At the home only, before the signature's deadline.
checks: A non-zero factory and configuration hash, and an amount above zero and at most `MAX_GRANT`.
The chain is a supported deposit chain: Ethereum, Avalanche, OP Mainnet, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon or HyperEVM.

For Arbitrum, the amount is added to the allowance at once if the factory is already trusted, or later by `applyAuthorisation`. For another chain it is only recorded here, for `dispatchAuthorisation`.
The allowance only grows by authorisations and only shrinks by funding.

applyAuthorisation.does: Adds an Arbitrum authorisation, made while its factory's trust was pending, to the allowance.
applyAuthorisation.when: At the home only, once the factory's trust is in effect.
checks: The authorisation exists, is for Arbitrum and has not been applied.
The trust in effect is the very one it was granted under: an authorisation made under a cancelled trust never applies, even if the factory is trusted again later.

dispatchAuthorisation.does: Sends an authorisation for another chain to this same address there, by a Circle message (finalized). The copy applies each id once, so sending it again is harmless.
dispatchAuthorisation.who: Anyone, as often as needed (a message lost or expired).
dispatchAuthorisation.when: At the home only, once the factory's trust is in effect.
checks: The authorisation exists and is for a chain other than Arbitrum.
The trust in effect is the very one it was granted under.

cancelTrust.does: Cancels a factory's pending trust for one chain, and with it every authorisation granted under that trust, for good. A trust lets the transfer key fund the contracts that factory says are this account's, within each amount signed for them; this contract does not check the factory's code, so a trust the owner did not mean is cancelled here within its 24 hours.
cancelTrust.who: The owner: signed by any credential in effect. No nonce: the message names the factory, the chain and the due time.
cancelTrust.when: At the home only, strictly before the trust takes effect, and before the signature's deadline. Once in effect, a trust is permanent; the pinned factory's trust on Arbitrum or HyperEVM is in effect at once, so it cannot be cancelled.

params.domain: The chain of the pending trust, by its CCTP domain number (Ethereum 0, Avalanche 1, OP Mainnet 2, Arbitrum 3, Base 6, Polygon 7, HyperEVM 19).

withdraw.does: Pays an amount of a token (zero: the chain's native coin) to the withdrawal address. When the owner's own wallet calls it, the flat 1 USD exit fee in the chain's USDC or its pinned USDT goes to the fee recipient; the transfer key's and the escape hatch's withdrawals pay no fee.
withdraw.who: A wallet credential in effect, calling from its own address; the transfer key unless the owner revoked it on this chain; and **anyone** once the deposit factory's transfer key has not checked in for 7 days (the escape hatch).
withdraw.when: Once a withdrawal address is in effect on this chain, and on a copy only while it is synced (its record sent by the home within the last 30 days). An unsynced copy refuses every caller, the escape hatch included (`NotSynced`), until the home's record arrives again.
checks: The destination is always the withdrawal address in effect: the caller chooses only the token and the amount.
On a copy whose record is older than 30 days, it reverts for every caller: a withdrawal never goes to an address the home has since replaced for longer than that.
The native coin can reach the address before the contract exists there, or be forced in; the contract refuses a plain transfer once it exists.

A wallet credential's own withdrawal of USDC or USDT, with a fee recipient set, must be above the 1 USD fee (`AmountNotAboveFee`: nothing moves), unless it is the whole balance, which then leaves free (so the owner can always empty the account). If the fee's transfer fails (a blacklisted recipient), the withdrawal goes ahead whole.
No caller but the owner pays a fee, so nobody can turn the owner's money into fees a dollar at a time.

params.token: The token to pay out; zero for the chain's native coin.
params.amount: How much of `token` to pay, in its smallest unit.

withdrawSigned.does: The owner's signed withdrawal: the signed amount leaves, the flat 1 USD exit fee (USDC or the pinned USDT, when a fee recipient is set) to the fee recipient and the rest to the withdrawal address.
withdrawSigned.who: The owner: a local action signed by a credential in effect, with that credential's own local nonce. Anyone may submit it; the submitter chooses nothing.
withdrawSigned.when: On any chain whose copy is synced (its record sent by the home within the last 30 days), before the signature's deadline. Revoking the transfer key does not stop it.
checks: Every field is signed: token, amount, destination, maximum fee, fee recipient.
The signed destination must still be the withdrawal address in effect, and the signed fee recipient the deposit factory's in effect: a signature played after either changed reverts.

For USDC and the pinned USDT the owner always signs a maximum fee of at least the 1 USD flat fee (`FeeAboveMax` otherwise, whether or not a fee turns out due); with a fee recipient set the amount must be above it (`AmountNotAboveFee`) unless it is the whole balance, which then leaves free. If the fee's transfer fails, the withdrawal goes ahead whole. Other tokens and the native coin pay none.

fund.does: Pays this chain's USDC to a strategy contract the owner authorised.
fund.who: The transfer key only, unless the owner revoked it on this chain.
fund.when: Once a withdrawal address is in effect here, since a strategy's exit pays it.
checks: The factory is trusted by this account for this chain.
The strategy contract exists (deployed before funded, its whole configuration validated by its factory) and the factory confirms it belongs to THIS account (`authorisedFor`).
The amount is within the allowance the owner signed for that factory, strategy and configuration, which it consumes.

params.vault: The strategy contract to pay: deployed, and registered to this account by `vaultFactory`.
params.amount: How much USDC to pay, in its smallest unit (6 decimals).

convertSwap.does: Swaps USDT for USDC in this chain's pinned Uniswap V3 pool (0.01%), paid to this account.
convertSwap.who: The transfer key only, unless the owner revoked it on this chain.
convertSwap.when: On Ethereum, Arbitrum and Polygon, the chains with a pinned pool.
checks: The minimum out is raised to at least the amount less 0.2% (998 USDC per 1,000 USDT); a tighter one asked for is kept.
The swap is on the pool itself, no router, and the account pays the pool only in its callback, during this call.

params.amountIn: How much USDT to swap, in its smallest unit (6 decimals).
params.minOut: The least USDC to accept; raised to the contract's own bound when lower.

uniswapV3SwapCallback.does: Pays the pinned pool the USDT it is owed for the swap in progress.
checks: Pays at most the swap's amount in, and once per swap.

params.amount0Delta: What the swap owes the pool (positive) or receives from it (negative) in the pool's first token.
params.amount1Delta: The same, in the pool's second token.

convertBurn.does: Burns this chain's USDC by Circle's bridge (CCTP V2, standard transfer), to be minted to this same address on another supported chain. Anyone may complete the mint there.
convertBurn.who: The transfer key only, unless the owner revoked it on this chain.
convertBurn.when: On a chain with Circle USDC.
checks: The destination is a supported deposit chain other than this one, and the recipient is always this same address.
The fee allowed is Circle's own minimum for the amount, read in the call, and a burn whose minimum is above 0.1% of the amount is refused.

Per UTC day, the fees of this chain's burns together stay within 0.1% of the highest USDC balance seen here at a burn that pays a fee that day; a burn beyond it reverts (`BurnFeeTooHigh`). A burn with no fee is not counted. A round trip never raises the balance above its earlier peak, so a stolen transfer key's round trips can pay Circle at most that much a day here, while a large deposit later in the day is never held back.
The token approval is exact and reset to zero after the burn.

params.amount: How much USDC to burn here and mint on the other chain, in its smallest unit (6 decimals).
params.destinationDomain: The deposit chain to mint on, by its CCTP domain number (Ethereum 0, Avalanche 1, OP Mainnet 2, Arbitrum 3, Base 6, Polygon 7, HyperEVM 19); not this chain.

burnMinFee.does: Circle's minimum fee for burning an amount on this chain (zero where the messenger has none).

params.amount: The amount to burn, in USDC's smallest unit.

conversionPool.does: This chain's pinned USDT to USDC pool and its two tokens (zeros where there is none).

returns.pool: The pinned Uniswap V3 USDT/USDC pool on this chain (zero where there is none: only Ethereum, Arbitrum and Polygon have one).
returns.usdt: This chain's USDT (zero where there is no pool).
returns.usdc: This chain's USDC (zero where there is no pool).

cctpUsdc.does: This chain's Circle USDC and Circle domain (zeros where the account burns nothing).

returns.usdc: This chain's Circle USDC (zero where the account burns nothing).

EXIT_FEE.does: The flat fee of an exit the owner makes (its wallet's own withdraw, or its signed withdrawal), in the chain's USDC or its pinned USDT: 1 USD, compiled, never settable. Other tokens and the native coin pay none. Only when a fee recipient is set; an amount at or below it is then refused, and when the fee's transfer fails the withdrawal goes ahead whole.

CODE_VERSION.does: This code's version in the factory's list: 1 for the genesis, n for the nth listed version. It is not the owner record's `version`, which an upgrade does not change.

UPGRADE_TTL.does: How long after the home published it a copy still follows an upgrade message: 3 days. An older one is ignored, and the home's current version is published again.

SCHEDULE_UPGRADE_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type hash of `ScheduleUpgrade(address implementation,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)`, a record change.

CANCEL_UPGRADE_TYPEHASH.does: The EIP-712 type hash of `CancelUpgrade(address implementation,uint256 due,uint256 deadline)`, a cancellation (no nonce).

UPGRADE_TAG.does: The tag of the home's upgrade message to a copy, `keccak256("dltx.owner-upgrade.v1")`; its format (tag, implementation, publishedAt) is frozen for every version.

module.does: This version's record module: the contract whose functions (the record changes, the copies, the upgrade) this account runs in its own storage. Created before this code, its code hash checked by the constructor; never changeable.

implementation.does: The code this account runs now (the ERC-1967 slot): the factory's genesis at deployment, then each version its owner moved it to.

pendingUpgrade.does: The pending upgrade, zeros if none: its target, the target's listed version and when anyone may apply it. It stays cancellable after that time, until it is applied.

returns.impl: The implementation the account will move to (zero: none pending).
returns.codeVersion: Its version in the factory's list.
returns.due: When anyone may apply it, as a Unix time in seconds.

removalPendingOf.does: Whether a credential has a removal proposed and not yet settled. Always false on a copy, where removals never happen. A strategy's upgrade path refuses such a credential as its scheduler.

fallback.does: Runs the record module's functions in this account's storage: the record changes and their cancellations, `publish`, Circle's message handlers, and the upgrade (`scheduleUpgrade`, `cancelUpgrade`, `applyUpgrade`, `publishUpgrade`). Any other selector is refused by the module.
fallback.who: Anyone may call; each function it runs applies its own rule on who may call it.
checks: It accepts no native coin.

scheduleUpgrade.does: Schedules the account's move to a later listed version of its code, applied by anyone 24 hours later unless a credential cancels it first. One upgrade is pending at most and is never replaced: to change the target, cancel, then sign again.
scheduleUpgrade.who: The owner: a record change signed by a credential in effect, with that credential's own record nonce; never DLTX, the transfer key or the recovery key.
scheduleUpgrade.when: At the home only, before the signature's deadline, while no upgrade is pending.
checks: The factory lists `impl` with a version above this one: forward only.
The signing credential has no removal pending.

params.impl: The listed implementation to move to.

cancelUpgrade.who: The owner: signed by any credential in effect, the scheduler included. No nonce: the message names the upgrade and its due time.
cancelUpgrade.when: At the home only, until the upgrade is applied (also after its due time), and before the signature's deadline.

applyUpgrade.does: Applies the pending upgrade: first every change already due lands under the current code, then the account's code moves to the target (`Upgraded`). If the credential that scheduled it is no longer in effect or has a removal pending, the upgrade is cleared instead (`UpgradeCancelled`).
applyUpgrade.who: Anyone; DLTX applies it once due and pays the gas.
applyUpgrade.when: At the home only, once the upgrade is due, never during one of the account's own money calls.

publishUpgrade.does: Sends the code this account runs now to this same address on another deposit chain, through Circle's message transmitter (no burn, no fee, finalized): the copy there follows it if its own factory lists that version and it is higher.
publishUpgrade.when: At the home only, as often as needed.

params.domain: The deposit chain's CCTP domain (not the home's).

Initialised.does: The account was created with its first owner set.

AdditionProposed.does: A credential's addition was proposed; it takes effect at `due` unless a current credential cancels it.

errors.NotFactory: `initialize` was not called by the factory.
errors.NotInitialised: Called on the implementation the accounts copy, which holds no record and serves no one.
errors.BadOwnerSet: The first owner set is not exactly one credential.
errors.BadCredential: A credential is malformed: an unknown kind, a zero wallet, or a key not on the P-256 curve.
errors.NotAllowed: The caller may not make this call: not the transfer key (or it is revoked), not a wallet credential, and the escape hatch is not open; or, for the swap callback, not the pinned pool during a swap.
errors.NotHome: A call only the home takes (a change to the owner record, an authorisation, or sending either to another chain) was made on a copy: the home is on Arbitrum.
errors.NotCopy: A record message reached the home, which sends records and never takes one.
errors.BadSignature: The signature is not from a credential in effect on this chain.
errors.BadNonce: The nonce is not the signing credential's next one.
errors.AlreadyMember: The credential is already in the record, or its addition is pending.
errors.NotMember: The credential is not in effect: a pending addition is cancelled, not removed.
errors.TooManyCredentials: The record already holds four credentials, pending additions counted.
errors.LastCredential: The removal would leave no credential standing, pending removals counted.
errors.AlreadyPending: The credential's removal is already pending.
errors.NothingPending: No pending change matches the one named (its credential, address or factory, and its due time), or it already took effect.
errors.SelfRemoval: A credential proposed its own removal: another credential must.
errors.SelfCancel: The credential being removed tried to cancel its own removal, which it may do only when that removal would leave it the last one standing.
errors.ZeroAddress: The proposed withdrawal address is zero.
errors.NoWithdrawalAddress: No withdrawal address is in effect on this chain yet.
errors.FeeAboveMax: A signed withdrawal of USDC or the pinned USDT named a maximum fee below the 1 USD exit fee.
errors.NotOwnVault: The strategy contract does not exist, or its factory does not register it to this account.
errors.NotTrusted: The factory is not trusted by this account for this chain (yet, or any more).
errors.AlreadyApplied: The authorisation's allowance was already added.
errors.AllowanceExceeded: The amount is above what the owner authorised for that strategy contract.
errors.ConversionUnavailable: This chain has no USDC for the account to pay or burn, or no pinned pool to convert in.
errors.BadDomain: The chain named is not a supported deposit chain, is this one, or does not fit the call (an authorisation for Arbitrum is applied, one for another chain dispatched).
errors.BadAmount: The amount is zero or out of range: an authorisation above the maximum grant or missing its factory or configuration, a swap too large, or a pool asking for more than the swap's amount.
errors.BurnFeeTooHigh: Circle's minimum fee for the burn is above 0.1% of the amount, or would take the day's fees on this chain above 0.1% of the highest USDC balance seen at a fee-paying burn that day.
errors.BelowMinimum: The swap would return less USDC than the minimum.
errors.TransferFailed: A token or coin transfer failed, or the token has no code.
errors.Reentered: A call re-entered the account while a payment was under way.
errors.NotTransmitter: A message handler was called by someone other than Circle's message transmitter.
errors.NotHomeMessage: The message does not come from this same account on Arbitrum.
errors.NotFinalized: The message was not attested at finality.
errors.BadMessage: The message is malformed: too short, of an unknown kind, or with an invalid record.
errors.NotSynced: This copy has not received the home's owner record, or the one it holds was sent more than 30 days ago (`RECORD_TTL`), so it cannot check a signature or let money leave until the home's record arrives again.
errors.NotWithdrawalAddress: The signed withdrawal names an address that is not the withdrawal address in effect.
errors.NotFeeRecipient: The signed withdrawal names a fee recipient that is not the factory's in effect.
errors.AmountNotAboveFee: An owner's withdrawal of USDC or the pinned USDT, with a fee recipient set, was at or below the 1 USD exit fee and not the whole balance: nothing moves, the money stays (the whole balance at or below the fee leaves free).
errors.BadModule: At construction: the record module has no code or not the code hash given.
errors.BadImplementation: An upgrade names an implementation this chain's factory does not list, or (at the home) one not above the account's version. At a copy the message reverts and stays relayable.
errors.RemovalPending: The credential scheduling an upgrade has a removal pending.
errors.NotDue: The pending upgrade's 24 hours have not passed.

contracts.name: DepositFactory
contracts.title: The deposit factory
contracts.brief: Creates each user's deposit contract, and holds DLTX's transfer key and offline recovery key for them.
contracts.summary: Creates each user's deposit contract, at an address computed from the user's id and their first owner set, the same on every chain, and holds DLTX's keys for them: the transfer key, which must check in daily, and the offline recovery key. Its constructor creates the genesis, version 1 of the deposit contract, on which every account is deployed; the recovery key alone lists later versions, behind a public 7-day delay, and each owner moves their own account. Its only constructor argument is the recovery key. It holds no money and names no strategy contract factory: each account trusts the factories its owner authorises.

STOP_AFTER.does: How long the transfer key may go without checking in before the escape hatch opens.

transferKey.does: DLTX's transfer key on this chain (zero until the recovery key sets it).

pendingRecovery.does: A successor the recovery key proposed, not yet accepted (zero if none).

feeRecipient.does: Where the fee of an owner-signed withdrawal goes; zero means no fee can be taken.

lastCheckIn.does: A version's last check-in: its listing until the first (the genesis: the factory's deployment).

saltOf.does: The CREATE2 salt of a user's account: the hash of their id and their first owner set, in order.

addressOf.does: A user's account address for this first owner set, deployed or not.

deploy.does: Creates a user's account with its first owner set, or returns it if it already exists.
deploy.who: Anyone, on any chain: whoever deploys it, the account starts with the user's own credentials, since they are part of its address.
deploy.when: Any time; the account's address can hold money before it exists.
checks: The owner set is exactly one well-shaped credential (a point on P-256 or a non-zero address), as `initialize` checks; any other set reverts, and nothing is created at its address.

setTransferKey.does: Sets or replaces the transfer key on this chain.
setTransferKey.who: The recovery key (the first setting, or a lost or stolen key), or the current transfer key itself (a planned rotation).
checks: A non-zero address.

Setting a key is not itself a check-in, but the recovery key can set a key it holds, which then checks in: the escape hatch protects against a DLTX that has gone, not against its recovery key. Your own signed withdrawal, or a wallet credential's `withdraw`, needs neither.

params.next: The new transfer key for this chain.

checkIn.does: Resets the escape hatch's 7-day clock of each version named.
checkIn.when: Daily, for each version DLTX still supports; a version's support ends by leaving it out. The genesis is checked in for the factory's whole life.
checks: Each version is listed.

stopped.does: Whether 7 days have passed without a check-in of a version: anyone may then have any account on that version pay its withdrawal address. True for a number not listed.

params.version: The version (an account asks its own `CODE_VERSION`).

setFeeRecipient.does: Sets where the fee of an owner-signed withdrawal goes; zero stops all fees.
checks: The recipient receives only fees the owner signed for, and a signed withdrawal naming a previous recipient no longer executes.

params.next: The new fee recipient; zero stops all fees.

proposeRecovery.does: Proposes the recovery key's successor; zero withdraws a proposal.

params.next: The proposed successor recovery key; zero withdraws a proposal.

acceptRecovery.does: Completes the handover: the proposed key becomes the recovery key.
acceptRecovery.who: The proposed successor only, which proves it can sign.

LISTING_DELAY.does: How long a proposed version waits before the recovery key may accept it: 7 days, public from its proposal.

MAX_SUCCESSIONS.does: The most factory successions between this factory and a listed version's own factory: 8.

predecessor.does: The factory this one continues: none (zero) for this one. A successor factory names its predecessor, which lets the predecessor list a version that names the successor.

genesis.does: Version 1 of the deposit contract, created by this factory's constructor: the code every account is deployed on, whoever deploys it and whatever is listed since.

proxyImplementation.does: What a proxy created by this factory runs first: always the genesis.

versionOf.does: The listed version of an implementation (1 for the genesis), zero for an unlisted address.

proposals.does: A pending listing: when the recovery key may accept it (zero: none) and the code hash it was proposed with.

implementationAt.does: The implementation of a listed version; reverts for a number not listed.

latest.does: The last listed version's implementation: what the web may offer once DLTX released it, never what `deploy` uses.

proposeImplementation.does: Proposes a later version of the deposit contract, acceptable 7 days later. Several proposals may run at once.
checks: The implementation has code, is not listed and not already proposed.
It names this factory as its own, or a later factory descending from it (each naming the one before as its predecessor, at most `MAX_SUCCESSIONS` steps), and so does its module.
Its `CODE_VERSION` is above every listed version, and its module's is the same (the account's forward-only check reads the module's).

acceptImplementation.does: Lists a proposed version, as the next number, and starts its check-in clock. Nothing ever removes a listed version.
acceptImplementation.when: At or after the proposal's due time, in version order.
checks: Its code hash is the one proposed.
Its `CODE_VERSION` is the next number.

Deployed.does: A user's deposit contract was created.

params.salt: The salt it was created with (`saltOf`).

params.next: The transfer key from now on.
params.by: Who changed it: the recovery key, or the transfer key itself.

CheckedIn.does: The transfer key checked a version in, restarting its escape hatch's 7-day clock.

params.at: When, as a Unix time in seconds.

params.next: The fee recipient from now on (zero: no fees).

RecoveryProposed.does: The recovery key proposed its successor.

params.proposed: The proposed successor (zero: a proposal withdrawn).

RecoverySet.does: The proposed successor accepted and became the recovery key.

params.next: The recovery key from now on.

ImplementationProposed.does: The recovery key proposed a later version: public 7 days before it can be listed.

params.codeHash: Its code hash, which acceptance checks again.

ImplementationListed.does: A version was listed: the genesis by the constructor, a later one by the recovery key's acceptance.

errors.NotAllowed: The caller is not the key this call needs: the recovery key, the transfer key, or the proposed successor.
errors.ZeroAddress: A key was set to zero, at deployment or after.
errors.DeployFailed: The deposit contract was not created at its expected address.
errors.BadImplementation: A proposal names an address with no code, an implementation or module of another factory, or code that changed since its proposal.
errors.AlreadyPending: The implementation is already proposed: no silent restart.
errors.NotDue: The proposal's 7 days have not passed.
errors.BadVersion: A version number out of order: a proposal not above the list, an acceptance not the next number, a check-in or `implementationAt` of a number not listed.

contracts.name: DepositProxy
contracts.title: The account proxy
contracts.brief: The fixed ERC-1967 proxy every deposit contract and every strategy contract is: it runs the code its owner chose, and has no function of its own.
contracts.summary: The fixed ERC-1967 proxy each user's deposit contract is, at the address its factory computes from the user's id and first owner set; each strategy's hub and legs are the same proxy, made by the combination factory. Its address never depends on the code it runs. It asks its maker, once, for the code to run first (the deposit factory's genesis), then delegates every call to the code in its ERC-1967 slot, which only the owner's upgrade moves. It has no admin and no function of its own.

fallback.does: Runs the call in the code the ERC-1967 slot names, in this contract's storage, and returns or reverts as that code does.
fallback.who: Anyone; the code it runs applies its own rules.
checks: Payable, so a later version may accept the native coin; version 1 of the deposit contract has no payable function, so a plain transfer reverts there.

Upgraded.does: ERC-1967's event: the proxy was created running this code.
